Verified half: a NAME no class declares -> the CobolObject root throws EC-OO-METHOD (probe out/probe/objects-p1/e_NOPE.cob: 'EC-OO-METHOD (fatal)'; conformance-test:OoSpineTests.Universal_UnknownMethod_EcOoMethod); for a TYPED receiver the not-found and non-matching cases are compile-time (COBOL0825 / 0828 under §14.9.23.3 SR4/SR5c), which is permitted. DIVERGING half: through a UNIVERSAL receiver the emitted __CobolInvoke binds the first class declaring the NAME and then treats a failed match (argument count, RETURNING presence, BY REFERENCE description — match rules 1 and 3) as a §14.9.23.4 GR7c conformance violation: EC-OO-UNIVERSAL when checking is enabled in both elements, otherwise an EC-less CobolImplementorFatalException. Under §9.3.6 the signature match is PART of resolution, so no match means step 6 -> EC-OO-METHOD, and GR7b (locate) precedes GR7c (conformance) in the GR7 execution sequence. Probes out/probe/objects-p1/e_ARITY.cob / e_RET.cob / e_DESC.cob all ended 'abnormal run-unit termination: INVOKE ... (ISO §14.9.23.4 GR7c...)' with NO exception name; expected EC-OO-METHOD. GR7c keeps content under this reading: it still governs ANY LENGTH formals and the §14.8.2/§14.8.3 residue that §9.3.6's match rules do not restate. The counter-reading (resolve by name only when overloading is not provided — §9.3.5.3 lets a PROVIDER of overloading choose its resolution methodology) is noted, but §9.3.6 itself is unconditional. Tests OoSpineTests.Universal_ArityMismatch_EcOoUniversal and Universal_ReturningPresenceMismatch_EcOoUniversal PIN the EC-OO-UNIVERSAL answer — a green test holding the gap open.
